fit.general_linear.params.statement: Parameters of the general linear fit t_c(p) over A, B, C

fit.general_linear.resid_pct.statement: Residuals (t_c - pred)/t_c x100 for A, B, C, general linear fit

fit.general_linear.max_abs_resid_pct.statement: Max |residual| of the general linear fit

fit.general_linear.dof.statement: Degrees of freedom of the general linear fit with 3 data points

fit.n_datapoints.statement: Number of independent (p, t_c) pairs available (A, B, C): any 2-parameter model has only 1 residual degree of freedom
fit.n_datapoints.detail: a 2-parameter fit to 3 points is only weakly constrained: it will look good (small residuals) almost regardless of the true functional form, because 2 of the 3 points fix the 2 parameters and only the third point carries information

pred.D.p_kgm2.statement: Chosen p for the hypothetical cylinder D: midpoint of p_B and p_C

pred.D.t_c_through_origin_s.statement: Predicted t_c of cylinder D from the through origin model

pred.D.t_c_power_law_s.statement: Predicted t_c of cylinder D from the power law model

pred.D.t_c_general_linear_s.statement: Predicted t_c of cylinder D from the general linear model

pred.D.model_spread_s.statement: Spread of the 3 model predictions for t_c(D): the dominant source of uncertainty

pred.D.geom_sensitivity_range_s.detail: much narrower than the spread between models (pred.D.model_spread_s): with only 3 cylinders, choosing the functional form matters far more than the geometric measurement uncertainty

pred.D.pD_lo_t_c_s.statement: Through-origin t_c(D) if p_D is shifted by -1 sigma

pred.D.pD_mid_t_c_s.statement: Through-origin t_c(D) if p_D is shifted by +0 sigma

pred.D.pD_hi_t_c_s.statement: Through-origin t_c(D) if p_D is shifted by +1 sigma

sigmaT.sg_gain_per_s.statement: Noise-gain factor of the 5-point order-2 Savitzky-Golay derivative: sigma_dTdt = this x sigma_T (iid noise on T)

sigmaT.formula.statement: Symbolic error chain: quadrature sum of (i) ADC quantisation referred to the thermocouple through the local calibration slope dT/dV and the amplifier gain G, (ii) the thermocouple calibration/polynomial uncertainty, (iii) the ice-point reference-junction uncertainty
sigmaT.formula.detail: each sigma is itself possibly T-dependent (dT/dV is, sigma_ADC is not); no cross-terms because the three sources are physically independent

sigmaT.sigma_ADC_uV.statement: ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY: half-LSB quantisation noise referred to the thermocouple, using the ASSUMED ADC (assume.adc_fs_V, assume.adc_bits) and the gain that spreads the run's span over ~1000 counts (qual.gain_for_1000_counts)
sigmaT.sigma_ADC_uV.detail: NOT a measured instrument spec: the true ADC/amplifier noise floor is not in the sources; if it is worse than assumed here, sigma_T scales linearly with it

sigmaT.sigma_T_ADC_hi_K.statement: ILLUSTRATIVE: sigma_T from ADC quantisation alone near 295 K (high sensitivity, dT/dV small)

sigmaT.sigma_T_ADC_lo_K.statement: ILLUSTRATIVE: sigma_T from ADC quantisation alone near 80 K (low sensitivity, dT/dV large -> worse)

sigmaT.sigma_dTdt_hi_Ks.statement: ILLUSTRATIVE: propagated sigma_dTdt near 295 K = sg_gain x sigma_T_ADC_hi

sigmaT.sigma_dTdt_lo_Ks.statement: ILLUSTRATIVE: propagated sigma_dTdt near 80 K = sg_gain x sigma_T_ADC_lo

sigmaT.crosscheck_vs_observed_noise_pct.statement: How far the ILLUSTRATIVE ADC-only sigma_dTdt near 80 K falls from the actually observed dT/dt noise floor on the plateau of run C (bal2.noise_std_dTdt_plateau_C_Ks)
sigmaT.crosscheck_vs_observed_noise_pct.detail: agreement to within a few tens of percent is a nontrivial cross-check that the assumed ADC/gain are in the right ballpark, NOT proof of the true spec

sigmaT.sigma_tc_halfsample_s.statement: sigma_t_c from finite sampling alone: since the collapse is sharp (peak/plateau ratio 5-11, run.frac), the identified peak sample changes only if the noise perturbation rivals the peak-to-neighbour drop; the residual uncertainty is +/- half a sample
sigmaT.sigma_tc_halfsample_s.detail: matches the <=3 s sensitivity-sweep spread already reported (tc.*.sens_t_spread_s): dominated by sampling, not by sigma_T

sigmaT.relQA_plateau_A_pct.statement: ILLUSTRATIVE relative Q/A uncertainty from sigma_dTdt alone on the film plateau of run A (dominant term there)

sigmaT.relQA_peak_A_pct.statement: ILLUSTRATIVE relative Q/A uncertainty from sigma_dTdt alone at the Q/A peak of run A (small: the signal is huge there)

sigmaT.relQA_plateau_B_pct.statement: ILLUSTRATIVE relative Q/A uncertainty from sigma_dTdt alone on the film plateau of run B (dominant term there)

sigmaT.relQA_peak_B_pct.statement: ILLUSTRATIVE relative Q/A uncertainty from sigma_dTdt alone at the Q/A peak of run B (small: the signal is huge there)

sigmaT.relQA_plateau_C_pct.statement: ILLUSTRATIVE relative Q/A uncertainty from sigma_dTdt alone on the film plateau of run C (dominant term there)

sigmaT.relQA_peak_C_pct.statement: ILLUSTRATIVE relative Q/A uncertainty from sigma_dTdt alone at the Q/A peak of run C (small: the signal is huge there)

stage.status.statement: Evidentiary status of each stage given this experiment (observed / indications only / not resolved), used verbatim in sec. 6

stage.bounds_dT_K.statement: ΔT boundaries used to shade stages VI/V/IV/III-II/I on cylinder C (right to left: 300(edge), 150(VI/V, arbitrary, matches the plateau window already used elsewhere), T_hi-77(V/IV, measured), T_lo-77(IV/III-II, measured), 5(III-II/I, arbitrary: below this Q/A is noise-dominated), 1(edge))
stage.bounds_dT_K.detail: only the IV/III-II and III-II-side boundaries (T_hi, T_lo) come from a measured feature; the VI/V and I edges are drawn where the report's own qualitative description already puts them and are not separately justified by a data feature

c1x.peak_Wm2_vs_window.statement: Peak Q/A of run C1 recomputed with different Savitzky-Golay windows (samples), everything else fixed

c1x.peak_window_spread_ratio.statement: Ratio of the largest to the smallest peak Q/A over window in {3,5,7,9,11}: the reported C1 peak is not resolution-independent
c1x.peak_window_spread_ratio.detail: the whole 296->77 K drop spans only ~6 samples (run.dt_s ~1.42 s over ~8.5 s), so the numerical derivative -- and hence the peak Q/A -- is itself window-dependent by a factor >2

c1x.n_samples_full_transition.statement: Number of samples spanning the ENTIRE 296 K -> <80 K transition of run C1

c1x.h_equiv_at_peak_Wm2K.statement: Equivalent heat-transfer coefficient at the SG-window-5 peak Q/A of C1, using an order-of-magnitude Delta T ~ 100 K

c1x.Bi_at_peak.statement: Biot number h Lc/k_Cu implied by that equivalent h, cylinder C (Lc = geom.C.Lc_m, k_Cu = 400 W/mK)
c1x.Bi_at_peak.detail: Bi ~ 0.05-0.1: not overwhelmingly >1, but no longer negligible either -- the lumped-body assumption is marginal, not clearly satisfied, during this specific transient

c1x.plateau_T_diff_K.statement: Plateau temperature of C1 minus that of C (bare): if the junction were reading a locally colder/wetted spot, a persistent offset would be expected here
c1x.plateau_T_diff_K.detail: the observed difference is comparable to the plateau's own noise level: the data neither support nor rule out the wetted-junction hypothesis
